articles.title: 'Ramayana' cinematographer Pankaj Kumar talks about about Sunny Deol's 'Hanuman' to be seen in the second part: 'Expectations are high'
articles.summary: Ramayana gave audiences two big surprises for the next part.
articles.body: Ramayana gave audiences two big surprises for the next part. Sunny Deol appears as Lord Hanuman in the post-credit scene, while Raghav Juyal is introduced as Meghnath, son of Ravana. While not much has been said about Juyal's role, Deol's introduction became the major talking point and raised excitement among fans.While audiences are curious about what his character will bring to the film, there is already some good news. The film's director of photography, Pankaj Kumar, recently shared that several “fabulous sequences” featuring Hanuman has been shot. He also feels that these moments will make watching the character on the big screen a great experience.Speaking with Variety India, Kumar said, “The expectations around Hanuman are immense. I know people want to see him on screen. We have already shot a lot of fabulous sequences involving Hanuman, and I can promise you that it's going to be great. It's going to be a great experience to watch him on the big screen.”Other than Meghnath and Hanuman, Ramayan part 2 will also introduce some more important characters such as Jambavan, Bali and Sugriv.Pankaj Kumar further explained that Ayodhya and Lanka were given very different looks in the film. The difference can be seen in their buildings, sets, clothes and colours. Ayodhya is shown with bright colours to give the kingdom a cheerful look. Lanka, on the other hand, has a darker style, where the team used black and gold.This change is also seen in the lighting. Kumar used darker lights and strong shadows for Lanka, while he kept Ayodhya scenes bright and clear. These choices were made from the start to make both kingdoms look different and show their unique nature on screen.Ramayana Part 1 stars Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Ravi Dubey, Arun Govil, Anupam Kher, Lara Dutta, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kajal Aggarwal and Indira Krishnan.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Javed Akhtar hails Lord Ram and reacts to Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana': 'Ram is not just a person, Ram is an ideal, a morality, Ram is a way of living; I haven’t watched the film yet'
articles.summary: Veteran lyricist and screenwriter Javed Akhtar has described Lord Ram as a figure whose values go beyond religion.
articles.body: Veteran lyricist and screenwriter Javed Akhtar has described Lord Ram as a figure whose values go beyond religion. Speaking on Tuesday, he said he has heard good reviews of Nitesh Tiwari’s ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’ but has not seen it yet. He also spoke about Hindi cinema’s formulaic approach and Sonia Gandhi’s new book.Javed Akhtar has not watched ‘Ramayana’ yetJaved Akhtar was at the launch of the Indian Performing Right Society (IPRS) music creator report when he shared his views. He said his daughter, filmmaker Zoya Akhtar, has watched the film and liked it.“I haven’t watched the film yet. My daughter (Zoya) has seen it, and she has been praising it; she praises things with great difficulty. I haven’t heard her praising me yet,” Javed Akhtar told PTI.Why his lyrics connect with peopleAmong his many hit songs, ‘Pal Pal Hai Bhaari’ from the 2004 film ‘Swades’ is still widely loved. One of its famous lines is 'Mann se Raavan jo nikaale, Ram uske mann mein hai.'When asked why his words moved audiences while the music of ‘Ramayana’ did not get a similar response, he answered with confidence. “The simple explanation is that I’m a good writer; let’s start from here. So, my line touches people.”Javed Akhtar says, 'Ram is a way of life'The 81-year-old writer also explained why Ram remains relevant. He said, "Ram is not just a person; Ram is an ideal, a morality, Ram is a way of living. Ram is a certain aesthetic, certain morality. So, when you look at it and appreciate it, it will touch your heart."He said, "Many people may be angry with me, but the essence of Ram runs in the blood of every Indian, irrespective of religion. While he is sometimes personified as an individual, he is far greater than that; he is a way of life."The Nitesh Tiwari film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Ram, Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi as Sita.Why Hindi films stay 'generic'Asked about the shortage of literary adaptations in Hindi cinema, Javed Akhtar said makers depend on safe formulas.“Earlier also, there used to be very low adaptation of literature into films. We’ve had ‘Devdas’, ‘Saheb Biwi Aur Ghulam’, and a few films; the rest were generic. Hindi movies are generic because they want to please everybody; they want people in Gujarat, Punjab, Karnataka and UP to like them,” he said.Citing his book ‘Talking Films’, he said Hindi cinema has built a culture of its own, far from real life.“I have mentioned in the book that we have a culture of states (in our country), and there is one more state, which is Hindi film. It is a state with its own culture and different architecture,” he said.“Like, I grew up in Lucknow, and I’ve never seen anyone in my life who calls his father ‘Abba Huzoor’. This happens only in films,” he added.About 'Ramayana'Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the film features Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Ravie Dubey, and more. articles.title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ box office collections Day 1: Advance booking for Robert Downey Jr and Chris Evans starrer crosses Rs 10 crore in India; tickets sell for over Rs 4,000
articles.summary: Marvel Studios’ ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ is off to a strong start at the Indian box office.
articles.body: Marvel Studios’ ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ is off to a strong start at the Indian box office. The film that opened advance bookings in India on Tuesday, has reportedly shot past the Rs 10 crore mark in opening-day pre-sales.As per box office tracking reports, the film has hit the milestone around 30 days before its theatrical release. Sacnilk reports that the film has sold approximately one lakh tickets across the national multiplex chains of PVR INOX and Cinepolis in just 19 hours since bookings opened.‘Avengers: Doomsday’ advance bookingsThe film’s opening-day pre-sales have already shot past the 24-hour advance collections of previous films like ‘Avengers: Endgame’ (2019), which earned Rs 8.27 crore, ‘Spider-Man: No Way Home’ (2021), which recorded an estimated Rs 6.56 crore and ‘Avengers: Infinity War’ (2018), which raked in an estimated Rs 5.02 crore.While ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ has made an impressive start, its advance bookings opened a full month before its release, thus giving it potential to grow in the weeks ahead. Meanwhile, previous Marvel blockbusters generally began selling tickets just a week before their theatrical debut.'Avengers: Doomsday' to cross ‘Avengers: Endgame’ record‘Avengers: Endgame’ also remains a major benchmark for the franchise in India. The film sold more than one million tickets on BookMyShow within its first 24 hours in 2019. ‘Doomsday’ has not reached that figure, but its early booking window has given fans considerably more time to secure tickets.‘Avengers: Doomsday’ records premium ticket pricesThe film's high ticket prices, estimated at Rs 4,200 at Cinepolis Seawoods in Nerul, has not hampered advance sales. The ticket is for a 4DX 3D screening scheduled shortly after midnight on opening day, with booking charges reportedly taking the final checkout amount to approximately Rs 4,300. The reported rate has exceeded premium ticket prices of recent releases, including ‘Ramayana’, ‘Oppenheimer’ and ‘Dhurandhar: The Revenge’.Expectations for have also reportedly been fuelled by the success of ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ earlier this year which not only crossed the Rs 500 crore mark in India, but also went on to hit the USD 2.5 billion mark at the worldwide box office. Robert Downey Jr.’s return to the franchise, this time as Doctor Doom, is another major draw for audiences.With a month still to go before its December 17 theatrical release, ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ advance bookings will now depend on whether the movie can sustain over the coming weeks.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Anne Hathaway Welcomes Baby No. 3 with Husband Adam Shulman
articles.summary: The married couple is already parents to sons Jack and Jonathan
articles.body:
Anne Hathaway is officially a mom of three!

The Devil Wears Prada 2 star welcomed her third baby with husband Adam Shulman

The married couple tied the knot in 2012

PEOPLE can confirm that The Devil Wears Prada 2 star, 43, welcomed her third baby with husband Adam Shulman .

The couple's new addition joins sons Jonathan, 10, and Jack, 6 .

The Mother Mary star first shared the exciting news that she was expecting her third baby on Friday, June 19. In a video on her Instagram , Hathaway could be seen wearing a flowy white dress as she walked into the frame with her arms in front of her stomach.

As the song "Baby I'm Yours" by Barbara Lewis played, Hathaway dropped her arms to reveal her growing bump. She smiled, hugged her stomach and ran out of frame. "x Baby, I'm yours x," she captioned the post.

A rep for Hathaway didn't immediately respond to PEOPLE's request for comment at the time.

In October, the Verity actress appeared on CBS Mornings and chatted about the psychological thriller and how she felt to be weeks away from adding another baby to her family.

"We're thrilled, we're overjoyed, but what we're really focused on right now is really taking in still being a family of four," said Hathaway.

"Because everything's going to change for us, but it's really going to change for our kids. And we're about to go through this beautiful threshold together," she continued. "So I'm just really like, soaking in what it's like to be in this unit — because my kids are older, you know? They're 10 and almost 7, so we've been this unit for a period of time. And touch wood, everything goes well with this one, that's going to change."

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

Hathaway kept her most recent pregnancy under wraps throughout an international promotional tour for the long-awaited The Devil Wears Prada sequel. An exclusive source shared with PEOPLE that she waited to disclose the news because she "was excited about the movie and wanted the attention to stay on the project," as well as to "reveal the pregnancy on her own terms."

After officially announcing the news, Hathaway appeared on Late Night with Seth Meyers and raved about how "amazing" her pregnancy had been so far. Hathaway also admitted that she was "shocked" to learn she was pregnant again.

"Oh, my gosh. It's amazing. It's amazing," she told host Seth Meyers of her pregnancy. "I mean, we knew what we were doing, but we were so shocked it worked."

"We were so shocked it went this way, so we're calling this one our buzzer-beater," Hathaway added with a laugh.

articles.title: Russell Brand Reportedly Furious After Prison Staff Seized His Hair-Loss Pills, Leaving Him At Risk Of Balding In 3-4 Weeks
articles.summary: Russell Brand is reportedly facing an unexpected personal frustration behind bars after prison authorities confiscated his hair-loss medication and specialis...
articles.body:
Russell Brand is reportedly facing an unexpected personal frustration behind bars after prison authorities confiscated his hair-loss medication and specialist shampoo.

The comedian, who is serving a 10-year-and-six-month sentence following his rape and sexual assault convictions, is said to be particularly concerned about losing his trademark hairstyle.

A hair transplant specialist has warned that noticeable shedding could begin within weeks of stopping his medication, although the timeline varies between individuals.

Russell Brand Reportedly Upset After Propecia and Special Shampoo Are Confiscated

According to a report, Brand became frustrated after prison officers refused to let him continue using Propecia tablets and Alpecin caffeine shampoo following his arrival at HMP Wandsworth.

A source told The Sun that the 51-year-old was particularly worried about losing his hair and had appealed to prison staff to let him keep using the products.

"He was kicking off because he's worried he's going to lose his hair. He takes Propecia pills for his hair, but he had them confiscated inside," the source claimed.

The insider added that officers considered the medication non-essential because it was being used for cosmetic purposes.

Prisoners undergo healthcare assessments when they arrive in custody, during which their existing medication is reviewed. Any treatment they receive must be approved and administered through the prison healthcare system rather than simply brought in from outside.

Brand has reportedly relied on the products for years. In 2010, he was photographed carrying a packet of Propecia 1mg tablets while stopping to sign an autograph for a fan.

Hair Specialist Explains How Quickly Brand Could Start Losing Hair

Speaking to The Mirror US , Dr Aziz Elgindi, an International Society of Hair Restoration Surgery-registered hair transplant surgeon at Harley Street Hair Transplant Clinics, explained what could happen if Brand is unable to resume his medication.

Propecia contains finasteride, which works by reducing levels of dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone associated with male pattern baldness.

Dr. Elgindi explained that the drug has a relatively short half-life and can leave the bloodstream within approximately 30 to 48 hours. However, its effects on the enzyme responsible for producing DHT can continue for longer.

"Because of this, your hair shedding will start again as early as 3-4 weeks after stopping Propecia, but typically starts again after 3-6 months and continues," he explained.

The specialist added that after approximately 12 months without treatment, a person's hair loss could return to the stage their genetics would otherwise have determined at that age.

This means Brand could experience anything from relatively minor shedding to more noticeable thinning, depending on his underlying pattern of hair loss.

Dr Elgindi also suggested that people concerned about maintaining their hair should discuss continued treatment with a medical professional rather than making changes without advice.

Russell Brand Moved To HMP Littlehey After Spending Time At Wandsworth

The reported dispute over his hair-loss products began after Brand entered HMP Wandsworth following his sentencing.

However, he was transferred on November 13 to HMP Littlehey, a Category C prison in Cambridgeshire that accommodates a large population of men convicted of sexual offenses.

His wife, Laura Gallacher, confirmed his new location in a message shared during the couple's Sunday "Service with the Brands" program.

Brand is reportedly being held in a single cell on E Wing. The reasons for his transfer have not been officially confirmed, although reports have suggested that concerns about his safety and his assessed escape risk may have influenced the decision.

HMP Littlehey offers inmates access to activities including yoga, football, indoor bowls and educational programs.

According to The Independent , the prison also provides vocational training and opportunities for prisoners to take part in structured activities as part of their rehabilitation.

Russell Brand's Prison Sentence Follows Convictions For Rape And Sexual Assault

Brand's reported concerns about his appearance come as he begins serving a lengthy prison sentence following his criminal trial at Southwark Crown Court.

On November 5, a jury found him guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others in connection with offenses committed between 2004 and 2009.

He was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison on November 9. He was also acquitted of two additional rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Brand denied the offenses and pleaded not guilty throughout the proceedings. He has continued to maintain his innocence following the verdict.

The Crown Prosecution Service said the evidence demonstrated how Brand had used his celebrity status and influence to pursue women sexually without regard for their wishes.

He is expected to serve a substantial portion of his sentence in custody before becoming eligible for release on license and will remain subject to sex offender notification requirements indefinitely.

Prison Message Creates Another Problem For The Convicted Comedian

Brand's hair concerns have emerged alongside a separate controversy involving his communications from prison.

In the November 15 video, he maintained that he was innocent of the crimes for which he had been jailed, saying: "As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening."

The statement prompted an investigation by the Ministry of Justice into whether he had breached prison communication rules by having his wife deliver a message intended for public release.

Reuters reported that government officials had warned prisoners could not bypass restrictions on media communications by asking family members to publish statements on their behalf.

The Prime Minister's spokesperson described the message as "clearly appalling" and said action would follow if Brand is found to have broken the rules.

articles.title: Alaíde Costa canta Fátima Guedes, Zé Renato, Joyce Moreno e Johnny Alf no álbum 'Meu vício na dor de amar demais'  | G1
articles.standfirst: Veja a capa do disco que será lançado em 27 de novembro com repertório inédito feito para a artista.
articles.summary: Veja a capa do disco que será lançado em 27 de novembro com repertório inédito feito para a artista.
articles.body:
Capa do álbum 'Meu vício na dor de amar demais', de Alaíde Costa — Foto: Fábio Audi / Divulgação

♬ Idealizada por Marcus Preto, a capa do álbum que Alaíde Costa lançará em 27 de novembro, “Meu vício na dor de amar demais”, expõe a cantora em bela e expressiva foto de Fábio Audi.

Terceiro título da trilogia idealizada por Emicida e Preto para Alaíde Costa, o sucessor dos álbuns “O que meus calos dizem sobre mim” (2022) e “E o tempo agora quer voar” (2024) será lançado onze dias antes do 91º aniversário da artista, nascida em 8 de dezembro de 1935.

O álbum “Meu vício na dor de amar demais” foi gravado pela cantora entre fevereiro e agosto no estúdio Da Pá Virada, em São Paulo (SP), com produção de Pupillo e dos dois criadores da tríade fonográfica.

O repertório é quase inteiramente inédito e composto para Alaíde Costa, mas inclui regravação de “Ilusão à toa” (1961), uma das canções mais conhecidas do pianista e compositor Johnny Alf (19 de maio de 1929 – 4 de março de 2010), com quem Alaíde sempre teve intensa afinidade musical. A propósito, a cantora estreia amanhã, 19 de novembro, em São Paulo (SP), show inédito em que aborda o repertório de Alf com o cantor e pianista Zé Manoel.

O trio de músicos do álbum “Meu vício na dor de amar demais” é formado por Fábio Sá (baixo), Leo Mendes (violão de nylon) e pelo próprio Pupillo na bateria e na percussão. Já os arranjos de cordas são assinados por Antonio Neves e Henrique Albino – os mesmos arranjadores dos dois álbuns anteriores da trilogia.

Com essa moldura instrumental, Alaíde Costa deu voz a dez músicas inéditas. Joyce Moreno é nome recorrente nesse repertório, assinando “Meu ofício” com Paulo César Pinheiro e “Distância” e “Calos, rugas” – música caracterizada como vinheta na costura do álbum – com Emicida.

Fátima Guedes – cantora e compositora com quem Alaíde já fez show eternizado em álbum ao vivo editado em 2011 – é a autora da canção “Solar”. Zé Renato e Chico César são os compositores parceiros de “Permanecer”.

“Pó de vidro” é composição do violonista João Camarero com letra de Paulo César Pinheiro. Já o samba-canção “A falta que não me faz” traz a assinatura de Adriana Calcanhotto.

Também compositora, a própria Alaíde Costa é a autora de duas músicas do álbum. “De repente” é composição da artista com Paulo César Ventura. Já “Só por isso eu vim” – faixa já adiantada em 6 de novembro como primeiro single do álbum – é parceria de Alaíde com Emicida.

Por fim, a música-título do álbum “Meu vício na dor de amar demais” é composição de Guilherme Arantes que ganhou letra de Nando Reis.

Diferentemente dos dois discos anteriores da trilogia, bancados pelos dois idealizadores da trinca fonográfica da gravadora Samba Rock Discos, o álbum “Meu vício na dor de amar demais” foi viabilizado com recursos financeiros do edital Natura Musical.

articles.title: MP investiga gastos de festival que teve show de Joelma em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Apuração busca esclarecer contratos, despesas e arrecadação do evento realizado em setembro, em Nortelândia, além de possível contratação duplicada de atração artística com recursos públicos.
articles.summary: Apuração busca esclarecer contratos, despesas e arrecadação do evento realizado em setembro, em Nortelândia, além de possível contratação duplicada de atração artística com recurso
articles.body:
Ministério Público de Mato Grosso (MPMT) investiga gastos de festival que teve show de Joelma por R$ 580 mil em Nortelândia (MT) — Foto: Reprodução

O Ministério Público de Mato Grosso (MPMT) investiga os contratos, as despesas e a arrecadação do 21º Festival de Praia de Nortelândia , município a 254 km de Cuiabá. O evento foi realizado em parceria com a Associação Cuiabana de Belas Artes (ACUBA) entre os dias 4 e 6 de setembro e teve a cantora Joelma entre as atrações.

O contrato para o show de Joelma foi firmado em maio de 2026, por meio de contratação direta da empresa J Music Editora e Produções Artísticas Ltda., no valor de R$ 580 mil. A apresentação foi realizada no dia 4 de setembro, às 22h30.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Prefeitura de Nortelândia, com a ACUBA e com a J Music Editora e Produções Artísticas Ltda., mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A investigação foi aberta em 6 de novembro pelo promotor de Justiça Alexandre Balas. Entre os pontos apurados está a possibilidade de uma mesma atração artística ter sido contratada com recursos do município e do governo estadual. O documento do Ministério Público não identifica qual seria a atração nem aponta valores relacionados à suspeita.

O acordo de cooperação atribuiu à ACUBA a execução das atividades culturais e artísticas, enquanto a prefeitura ficou responsável por parte da estrutura, da logística e da segurança do evento.

O pagamento do show de Joelma foi dividido em duas parcelas de R$ 290 mil. Registros disponíveis no Portal da Transparência da Prefeitura indicam que a primeira parcela foi paga em 1º de setembro. Entre os registros consultados, não foi localizado comprovante da segunda parcela. O contrato previa que o valor restante fosse pago até 48 horas antes do show.

Além do cachê, o Portal da Transparência registra outras despesas relacionadas ao evento, como serviços de vigilância, hospedagem, alimentação e estrutura . Os valores identificados nesses registros somam R$ 34,8 mil, além da primeira parcela do contrato de Joelma.

O acordo com a ACUBA não prevê repasse financeiro direto da prefeitura à associação. Pelo documento, o município assumiu despesas como manutenção e limpeza do espaço, energia, água, segurança, atendimento de saúde, hospedagem e alimentação de artistas e equipes. A associação ficou responsável pela execução das atividades culturais e artísticas.

O regulamento do festival também previa a arrecadação de patrocínios, além de receitas com a locação de tendas e a concessão do bar. O documento autorizava o uso de recursos municipais caso essas fontes não fossem suficientes, mediante justificativa técnica e adequação orçamentária.

Os registros consultados não permitem identificar o custo total do festival nem o montante efetivamente arrecadado com patrocínios, tendas e bar.

A programação musical ocorreu na Praia Rota do Sol. No primeiro dia do evento, se apresentaram Cícero Edson, Joelma, Banda Tome Aí e o DJ Iannk Teles. Já no segundo dia, foi a vez da Banda Palladium, de Gilson Mark & Juliano e do DJ Iannk Teles. No terceiro e último dia do evento, subiram ao palco DJ Iannk Teles, Rodriguim Santana e o grupo Kamisa 10.

articles.title: 'Scene' box office collection day 12: Suriya, Naslen starrer surpasses 'Vishwanath and Sons'; earns Rs 252.45 cr worldwide
articles.summary: Suriya and Naslen's 'Scene' has maintained its box office momentum, taking its worldwide gross collection to Rs 252.45 cr in 12 days.
articles.body: Suriya and Naslen's 'Scene' has maintained its box office momentum, taking its worldwide gross collection to Rs 252.45 cr in 12 days. The Tamil-Telugu thriller earned Rs 2.90 cr net in India on Tuesday, November 17. Its latest earnings came from 4,011 shows across both language versions. The film's cumulative domestic net collection has reached Rs 142.40 cr, while its India gross stands at Rs 165.45 cr.According to Sacnilk reports, the film collected another Rs 1 cr from overseas territories on Day 12. This pushed its international gross collection to Rs 87 cr. With the combined domestic and overseas earnings, the Suriya and Naslen starrer is now approaching the Rs 300 cr worldwide milestone. Its performance has also put it ahead of Suriya's previous release, 'Vishwanath and Sons', in the worldwide collection comparison.'Scene' maintains its second-week box office runThe film registered a 3.3% decline in India net collections compared to the previous day's earnings. The Tamil version remained the primary contributor, collecting Rs 2.05 cr through 2,781 shows. The Telugu version added Rs 85 lakh from 1,230 shows. Together, the two versions generated the day's domestic earnings.During its second week, 'Scene' accumulated Rs 30.70 cr net, with the corresponding gross reaching Rs 35.70 cr. Its opening week had delivered Rs 111.70 cr net and Rs 129.75 cr gross across seven days. The film's cumulative domestic figures have now crossed another major milestone, while its Day 12 earnings translated to an average of approximately Rs 7,230 per show.Tamil version dominates language-wise collectionsThe Tamil version continues to account for the largest share of the film's domestic business. Its cumulative India net collection has reached Rs 114.15 cr, representing 80.2% of the total. The Telugu version has contributed Rs 28.25 cr, accounting for the remaining 19.8%.The Tamil 2D version recorded an overall occupancy of 23.29% in the detailed tracking figures. Morning shows registered 16.46%, while afternoon screenings recorded 22.31%. Evening and night shows reported 26.46% and 27.92%, respectively.Meanwhile, the Telugu 2D version registered 15.19% overall occupancy. Its morning shows recorded 10%, followed by 14.36% in the afternoon, 13.73% in the evening and 15.55% at night. The broader language-wise tracking figures placed Tamil occupancy at 20% and Telugu at 19%.Tamil Nadu emerged as the largest contributor to the film's tracked state-wise gross collections. The state generated Rs 1.50 cr, accounting for 44.8% of the day's tracked gross. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana together contributed Rs 85 lakh, while Karnataka added Rs 40 lakh.Kerala generated another Rs 55 lakh, and the remaining Indian territories contributed Rs 5 lakh. Together, these markets recorded a state-wise gross of Rs 3.35 cr. The overall revenue distribution also highlights the film's overseas performance. The film's Hindi shows contributed the largest share, earning Rs 21 crore from 17,867 shows. The language accounted for 73.2 per cent of the film’s Day 13 domestic net collection.The remaining collections came from four other languages. Malayalam brought in Rs 2.35 crore from 1,070 shows, followed by Kannada with Rs 2.10 crore from 894 shows. This brings its worldwide gross collection to Rs 1,483.50 crore.‘Ramayana’ Week 1 vs Week 2 performanceThe film scored an estimated first-week collection of Rs 564.60 crore net and approximately Rs 675.05 crore gross. Now in its second week, ‘Ramayana’ has collected Rs 310.20 crore net in India so far.With its worldwide gross nearing Rs 1,500 Crore, the film is on the verge of joining an exclusive club. Once it crosses the milestone, ‘Ramayana’ will become only the fifth Indian film to achieve the feat in the fastest time.'Ramayana' overseas collectonsAccording to a report on PTI, the studio has expanded its overseas release from an initial 37 markets to 43 markets, with six additional territories opening last weekend.The film, bankrolled by Namit Malhotra's DNEG and Prime Focus Studios in association with actor Yash's Monster Mind Creations, recorded openings of USD 573,000 (Rs 5.4 crore) in Indonesia and USD 286,000 (Rs 2.7 crore) in Cambodia, which the makers said were records for an Indian film in those markets. articles.title: Did Nicolas Cage Really Gain 60 Pounds to Play John Madden? He Says...
articles.summary: Nicolas Cage's transformation for Madden—the biopic in which he plays the legendary NFL coach while costarring with Christian Bale—included putting on 25 pou...
articles.body:
Nicolas Cage refuses to fumble a role by not looking the part.

After all, the National Treasure alum put on weight in addition to wearing a heavy bodysuit while portraying famed Oakland Raiders coach John Madden instead of relying on "a frozen mask of prosthetics."

"Sort of a hybrid of gaining weight—I gained about 25 pounds and added some prosthetics to achieve a 60-pound look," Cage exclusively told E! News' Will Marfuggi at the Madden premiere. "Enough of myself where I could still be expressive."

And though the dramatic body transformation brought the Longlegs actor closer to walking in on the late 85-year-old's cleats, that doesn't mean Cage didn't put his own artistic spin on the character.

"I'm not an impressionist. I lean more towards being a surrealist," the Oscar winner explained. "I'm trying to find the energy, the imagination, the heart of the man and dig deep within and try to inform it with something that is emotionally accurate."

Still, the 62-year-old—who attended the film's debut ahead of its release on Prime Video and in select theaters Nov. 18 with wife Riko Shibata , 31—studied Madden's "cadence and some of his gestures" to bring authenticity to his interpretation of the NFL legend.

In his words, Cage's game tape ahead of shooting entailed "a lot of reviewing interviews that he gave, and watching his announcing, and watching some old footage of him on the football field."

And while the Leaving Las Vegas star took hold of the character with both hands, he still managed to leave his work on the field while filming, so that he could focus on being dad at home to their 4-year-old August , who is the youngest of Cage's brood that also includes sons Weston , 35, and Kal-El , 21, from prior relationships.

"I think I left it on the set," he said, referencing one of his previous projects as he added, "I would come home and put the other hat on and be The Family Man ."

Aside from appreciating his wife's respect for his creative process, Cage praised his onscreen best friend Christian Bale —also lauded for his shocking physical metamorphoses in films like The Dark Knight , Fighter and Vice throughout his career—for being both an actor and an artist.

"That was really the heart of the movie," the Ghost Rider alum confessed of their chemistry. "It was the second time I'd worked with Christian. We did a picture a million years ago called Captain Corelli's Mandolin . So it was nice to have some more scenes to do with him."

As for whether Cage—a comic book lover who co-created his own series—nerded out in the presence of Batman, Bale's most powerful role?

"Not at all," Cage quipped. "Didn't come up in a single bit."

And the Madden costars are among other A-listers who have gone above and beyond to tackle a role. Run it back to these award-worthy performances...

Andra Day, The United States vs Billie Holiday

Hilary Swank, Boys Don't Cry & Million Dollar Baby

He also recalled Mammootty's reassuring words and thanked everyone who stood by him during his health crisis.An emotional meeting with MammoottyKannan visited the shooting location of Mammootty's film 'Mela' at Panangad to meet the actor. Although he had seen Mammootty at a shooting location years ago, this was his first opportunity to meet him closely and speak with him. articles.title: Jennifer Lopez says her four marriages were like ‘Learning the same thing over and over’ as she reflects on her split from Ben Affleck and her journey of self-discovery
articles.summary: Jennifer Lopez speaks about her mental state after her separation from the ‘Good Will Hunting’ star Ben Affleck.
articles.body: Jennifer Lopez speaks about her mental state after her separation from the ‘Good Will Hunting’ star Ben Affleck. Reflecting on her marriage, Lopez said it “was like learning the same thing over and over,” during a conversation with the SiriusXM studios. The ‘Wedding Planner’ actress has been married and divorced four times: to Ojani Noa, Cris Judd, Marc Anthony (with whom she shares 18-year-old twins Max and Emme), and most recently, Affleck.What Jennifer Lopez learned from her marriages?"It took me a minute to get it. And it’s fine,” she added about what she’s learned from past relationships. “Because I think that there was love that was involved and there was heartache and there were lessons. And you really realise it doesn’t matter what people do to you or any of that.What matters is what you’re doing in it or how you got there and figuring it out yourself. Like, it was really about figuring out myself every single time.” “You have six more fingers”, an audience shouted after Lopez talked about her getting married and divorced four times at the event. “That was the funniest thing I’ve ever heard in my life,” Lopez told SiriusXM hosts Nicole Ryan and Ryan Sampson.Jennifer Lopez reflected on her former husbandsWhile she was asked if she believes each of her ex-husbands came into her life “for a reason,” the 'On the Floor' singer reflected on lessons learned. “Having recently gone through [a divorce] a couple of years ago, it really felt like it was such a growth spurt for me,” Lopez explained.“I just delved into, like, ‘You know what? I need to figure out what I’m doing here.’ I felt like I did when the kids were born, but there’s another piece, or a few pieces, that I’m not getting. And I just haven’t got it yet. It’s okay, this is a long life.”What Jennifer Lopez’s therapist told her?She continued, “I had a therapist who told me — I was like, I just feel like, we all feel like sometimes we’re like— I’m f---ing everything up, you know? … He was like, ‘You’re so young. Just keep going. Keep discovering yourself and learn to love every part of yourself in that way. Even the parts that are the hopeless, romantic, and all of that.’”Rather than “blame that side of myself for things,” Lopez said she realised, “No, that’s the artist in me. That’s the dreamer in me. That’s the person who creates the things that I get to create. That’s the brave person who gets out in front of 50,000 people and dances around and does flips live on air.”“You have to be a little bit crazy. You know what I mean?” She laughed while saying this.The timeline of Jennifer Lopez’s marriage and separation from Ben AffleckJennifer Lopez, better known as J.Lo, is an American singer, actress, dancer, and businesswoman born on July 24, 1969, in the Bronx, New York. She first caught attention as a dancer on the TV show ‘In Living Color’ before breaking out as an actress in the 1997 biopic ‘Selena’ and building a huge music career with hits like ‘If You Had My Love’ and ‘Jenny from the Block.’She and Ben Affleck first dated in the early 2000s, then rekindled their romance in 2021, according to InStyle and married in Las Vegas on July 17, 2022, followed by a second anniversary of the traditional wedding ceremony in Georgia. They separated in late April 2024, and Lopez filed for divorce on August 20, 2024, as reported by People, exactly two years after their Georgia wedding.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Cambridge Dictionary chooses ‘human’ as word of the year in response to AI fears
articles.summary: Fears of artificial intelligence inspired the Cambridge Dictionary to flip back to the 15th century for the word that best captures the 2026 cultural zeitgeist.
articles.body: LONDON — Fears of artificial intelligence inspired the Cambridge Dictionary to flip back to the 15th century for the word that best captures the 2026 cultural zeitgeist. “Human,” the dictionary’s word of the year, is not just a throwback but also a backlash of sorts that reflects the debate over how AI has blurred the lines between machines and people. “AI is changing how we talk about being human,” said Colin McIntosh, the dictionary’s lexicographer. “Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children.” The adjective derived from the Latin “humanus” and in use since the 1450s is defined by Cambridge as “having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines.” Dictionaries typically choose a novel word — sometimes slang that has crossed into the mainstream — or an existing word that has taken on a new meaning. Artificial intelligence has factored heavily in Word of the Year distinctions across several dictionaries in recent years. “AI” itself was chosen by Collins Dictionary in 2023 — a year when Cambridge picked “hallucinate,” in reference to the tendency of AI to fabricate information. Merriam-Webster last year named “slop” its word of the year for low quality content produced by AI while Collins went with “vibe coding” for the AI-assisted software development method. “AI is making us think harder about what it means to be human,” Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, who has promoted the smart use of AI, said in a comment on the Cambridge Dictionary selection. “The measure of AI’s success should be how much it improves human lives.” Other word contenders for 2026 included “agent,” for an AI system that can make decisions and operate without human control and “analogue” for experiences or objects not involving the internet or digital technology.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos says he was ‘heavily involved’ in picking the new James Bond
articles.summary: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos told an audience that he was “heavily involved” with casting Robert Pattinson to play the new James Bond, saying that  he displayed “something special.”
articles.body: Tech billionaire and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has said that he was “heavily involved” with casting the new James Bond, telling an audience on Tuesday night that actor Robert Pattinson had displayed “something special.” Amazon MGM Studios assumed creative control of the blockbuster franchise last year, tapping Denis Villeneuve to direct its first instalment. In a rare peek into the casting of the iconic British spy, Bezos pulled back the curtain on the selection process that ultimately saw Pattinson announced as 007 to much global fanfare on Monday. “We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday,” Bezos told Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event in California. A “big group” of contenders were whittled down to five finalists who went through “real, old-fashioned screen tests” Bezos said. He added that the contenders each acted out three different scenes with “full costume, real sets, other actors with them,” to help with the casting process. Bezos did not name the finalists, but actors who reportedly tested for the role included Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult. Bezos said that he and a team, including the movie’s director Villeneuve, spent hours reviewing the finalists on Friday, noting that they were all “extraordinarily talented.” But he said “there was something special about Rob and his performances ... It was immediately un-debated,” he added. “We all gravitated toward Rob.” Pattinson said playing the suave British spy was “the honour of a lifetime.” In a statement on Monday, he added, “to say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.” With a career spanning more than two decades, Pattinson took to the screen as a teenager playing vampire Edward Cullen in the “Twilight” movies and Cedric Diggory in the “Harry Potter” franchise. A distinctive and versatile actor, he went on to pivot between smaller independent films and mega-studio productions including “The Batman.” Pattinson also recently enjoyed a viral turn as villainous Antinous in Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster “The Odyssey,” and played a shapeshifting assassin in “Dune: Part Three,” which saw him work with director Villeneuve. The script for the new Bond film is being written by Steven Knight, who created the British television series “Peaky Blinders.” No release date has yet been given for the new movie. Bond has evolved into one of the most coveted and discussed roles in film, with the book-to-screen character written by Ian Fleming displaying rare staying power across generations. “I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey ... but there can only be one 007,” director Villeneuve said in a statement this week. “I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new.” The six previous Bond actors — Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig — were little-known or drawn primarily from stage and small-screen work before being catapulted into fame as the secret agent. Bezos said initially the casting team had been “slightly biased” against Pattinson because he is “already so famous” and said they had been seeking “somebody a little more unknown.” Ultimately, he added, “in the screening tests, it was so obvious, he is James Bond.”

articles.title: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond. Can he become the hero the West needs?
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond, but can the "Twilight" and "Batman" star match Sean Connery's manly bearing as 007 in a West that needs a hero?
articles.body: So, Amazon MGM Studios announced that it chose the British actor Robert Pattinson to be the new James Bond. This could be bigger than mere new films in the franchise, as Ian Fleming’s creation was never more important for the Western psyche than now — in this time of political division in America and a weak and troubled Europe, the West needs its myths and heroes. But can Pattinson really be Bond? Bond is an old-school ultimate man’s man. He dresses above occasions, is cool under pressure, is a lady’s man, a secret agent and spoiler of the plots of terrorist masterminds. At 40, Pattinson is the right age to play the long-running and, arguably, the most iconic man’s man in film history. Sean Connery was just 32 years old when his first Bond film, "Dr. No," came out. But Pattinson is no Connery. IDRIS ELBA REJECTS 'WOKE' JAMES BOND CASTING PUSH, WARNS AUDIENCES 'WON'T GO FOR A BLACK MALE' IN THE ROLE Pattinson has the looks, almost, but he is more emblematic of a weak Timothy Dalton than the unforgettable Sean Connery or even of Roger Moore. Still, he is more of a Bond than Daniel Craig, an actor never stately or commanding enough to carry the role. Disappointingly, like Craig, Pattinson has expressed anti-gun sentiments. In interviews promoting the 2014 film "The Rover" (in which his character uses a gun), Pattinson said he was "quite anti-gun." But that was a long time ago and Pattinson has since been careful not to express political positions. This is good, as we don’t need more divisive political rhetoric from actors who are seemingly embarrassed by their roles. Pattinson’s casting followed screen tests and competition from actors reportedly including Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden. Given those choices, it is not hard to see why Pattinson stood out, even though his roles in "Harry Potter" and the "Twilight" films were boyish, not Bond-like. Sean Connery’s Bond set the standard of the tall, dark-haired, impeccably tailored agent who could effortlessly go from a tuxedo to a wetsuit. This character is supposed to be both suave and understated, and very few can carry both off at once. Bond’s lines are supposed to be dry and straightforward. He is never weak, though he can be captured and beaten. WHAT DO YOU THINK? NEW JAMES BOND IS ROBERT PATTINSON The official teaser for the next 007 film to come does not include a single word, just Pattinson, gun in hand, emerging from blackness with the iconic Bond theme strumming. This tells us nothing, but it is on theme. Pattinson shares key physical attributes with Connery — he is tall, has dark hair and an ability to look sharp in a tux. But can Pattinson look cool under pressure while emanating the danger of a lion in the tall grass? JAMES BOND LEGEND ROGER MOORE'S SON CALLS OUT TIKTOK CULTURE, HOLLYWOOD'S RECYCLED COMIC BOOK MOVIES I am hopeful, but previous roles never showed that Pattinson has the acting range or the manly bearing needed to pull this off. In "The Batman" (2022), Pattinson showed he could carry himself in a larger-than-life role, and he had the poise to make the part believable, but again the strength was not there. He is too weak-chested and never quite gives the impression he is as sure of himself as Bond must be — Frank Sinatra, for example, had this quality. 'PRIMETIME' STAR ROBERT PATTINSON SHOCKS FANS WITH CHRIS HANSEN TRANSFORMATION IN 'UNSETTLING' TRAILER So, OK, there can never be another Connery; therefore, the comparison is not quite fair. Then, can Pattinson carry the part forward into something this generation needs? So many today prefer to apologize for or ignore the Western canon that produced a fictional hero like Bond — a man willing and able to risk his life to save us. The official teaser for the next 007 film to come does not include a single word, just Pattinson, gun in hand, emerging from blackness with the iconic Bond theme strumming. This tells us nothing, but it is on theme. James Bond, at his best, is sophisticated, but hardly a snob. He has what the Spanish call duende, a characteristic author James Michener said is almost indefinable, as it means something with taste, refinement, beauty, perfection and elegance all in just the right proportion and with no showiness at all. He is what the Japanese mean when they use the word shibui, which is something a samurai tried to embody, but only could manage in fleeting moments when life and art meet before again separating with a bad gesture or misstep. JUDI DENCH BLASTS 'TRIGGER WARNINGS' RUINING STORIES, 'DRIVES ME WILD' In other words, James Bond is an archetype of what men wish they could be in the moments they are needed. Cool under pressure, not afraid to act or to fail and confident they are fighting for something good. This, again, is not something Hollywood has given us enough of today. articles.title: ‘It’s a risk’: How Rockstar built the most detailed (and romantic) GTA yet
articles.summary: Rockstar’s Rob Nelson talks about the long and detailed development of Grand Theft Auto 6.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t just the biggest GTA game to date; it’s also the most romantic. Though the series is well known for its sordid assortment of criminal leads, GTA VI switches things up by starring a pair of thieves who also happen to fall in love after meeting while stealing a car. It’s still an open-world action game full of chaos and mayhem. But many players will also be attempting to nurture the budding relationship in between heists. The sprawling game is designed to support both audiences. “It’s a risk,” explains Rob Nelson, producer on GTA VI and co-studio head at developer Rockstar North. “It’s a real change for Grand Theft Auto. You can still play it the old way, you can reject all of this stuff. But for people who do engage, it’s meaningful — you’re earning it, you’re working at it, just like in a normal relationship.” Despite the couple — named Jason and Lucia — being so central to the GTA VI experience, the development of the game didn’t start with characters or story. It began with a place. Nelson says that “pretty quickly” the team settled on placing the game in Leonida, the GTA universe’s version of Florida and the setting of one of the series’ most iconic games, Vice City on the PS2. In 2015, a small group of developers from Rockstar headed to Florida to get a sense of the place and set the groundwork for what would go on to become GTA VI. “We just went around to feel it out,” explains Nelson. “Go to the Everglades, go to the Keys, go to the city, as many places as we can, and start thinking about what aspects of the place we want to incorporate. And then the map team starts building our version of that and talking very loosely and very broadly about what types of people we want to include and what types of places.” The team realized they wanted to tell a story that would pull players through the various locations they were creating. And the best way to do that was to have characters who were relatively small-time criminals. They would start near the bottom of the criminal underworld and work their way up, traversing Leonida’s various locations, culminating in the splashy Vice City. [Image: At the same time, the developers also wanted to do something different with the character-switching mechanic from GTA V, which let players swap between three unique criminals, each with very different stories and motivations. For GTA VI, a couple working together to steal enough money to escape the outlaw life fit both of these ideas perfectly. But it also presented some new challenges. “Could we make a relationship work?” Nelson remembers thinking. “It’d be very different from three characters living separate lives that come together for narrative purposes and then split. These two are going to need to be together all the time and that’s going to be a challenge. It felt really wrong to have these people that are supposedly together only be together when we’re giving you scripted content.” While GTA V is the obvious reference point, the new GTA also builds off of Rockstar’s 2018 Western Red Dead Redemption 2. That game was notable in particular for giving players more ways to interact with the world: You could talk to any NPC, sit around a campfire while drinking coffee or playing cards, or grow out your beard for a new look. GTA VI expands this in ways that are designed to reinforce the relationship aspect of the experience. For instance, not only can you drink coffee, but you can also make a cup and hand it to your partner. The two can spend time together sitting on the couch watching TV, or go out to a club and dance. There’s even a button dedicated exclusively to making Jason and Lucia hold hands when they’re together. Nelson notes that when the team implemented the hand-holding feature, it was a revelatory moment for showing how the story and gameplay could connect. “When we got that mechanic in — and it’s not just a toggle, it’s an active thing that you have to commit to and hold — it was a really profound thing,” he says. But it’s also a careful balancing act. While RDR2 was a widely praised game, it also received criticism for its slow pace, which was due in large part to all of the small mechanical details. These added animations and button prompts that gave texture to the world but could also lead to a plodding pace. That would be a much bigger problem in a game like GTA, which is built around action. Nelson says that he can be “freakishly obsessive” about these kinds of details, but he and the team had to learn to let go when realism got in the way of the game itself. “Maybe you don’t have to carry around antifreeze in your trunk so that if your engine starts smoking you can top it up,” he says. “Certain things fall by the wayside in developing the game, where it’s like, we don’t need this. But other things, like eating food, it was important for us. You want to feel like you are this person existing in this world to a degree. That felt like it was additive. I love walking down the street with a beer and a cigarette and switching between the two, feeling like a dude. If it’s additive, and it makes you laugh, we include it.” [Image: This also led the team down some unexpected paths. For instance, GTA VI is the first game in the series with functioning bedsheets. In past titles, and in basically every other video game, characters simply lay on top of a bed to go to sleep. That’s because it’s a lot of effort to both animate a character going under the covers as well as rig the sheets so that characters can interact with them in a way that looks and feels natural. The payoff isn’t worth it. But in the context of GTA VI, where the characters hide out together in everything from dingy motel rooms to fancy hotels, it made sense to actually build it. “Because you’re sharing a living space, and you come in and see your partner sleeping at 3AM, it’s weird to see them laying on the top of the bed all the time,” Nelson says. “Nobody does that. It’s a lot of work to rig the covers on all of the different beds and have them both be able to get in and out of it and be able to be under the covers together.” Bedsheets, holding hands, cups of coffee — they’re seemingly small details in a world as large as Grand Theft Auto VI, one that encourages players to run wild. But they’re also indicative of the approach Rockstar took with this latest GTA and how the studio attempted to make every element work in concert, even if it required a lot of extra work, like the bed covers. “That’s an example of something that was a lot of work, but it was worth it.”

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived
articles.summary: More than 13 years after GTA 5, its sequel, GTA 6, is finally here.
articles.body: More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possibly the most anticipated video game launch of all time. Part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years. Some of it has to do with the sheer length of time between releases, a period that was plagued by leaks and a handful of delays that made the wait even harder for fans. But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here. That includes our own review and interviews with the development team, as well as news on just how the game ends up resonating with players.

articles.body: Chris Harrison believes young people are turning away from dating apps and looking toward faith as they search for meaningful relationships. The television host, who returned to reality dating television with the premiere of "Chris Harrison's The Vow" on Fox Nation, told Fox News Digital that he and the show's producers have noticed what he describes as a growing movement among younger generations seeking something deeper than modern dating culture offers. 'CHRIS HARRISON’S THE VOW’ SPARKS ‘TRAD WIFE’ DEBATE AMONG CONTESTANTS AS EMOTIONS RUN HIGH "Attending youth nights in incredible numbers at churches and temples and all these organizations getting together around faith. So clearly they're searching for something, looking for something, and at the same time, dating apps are being rejected." "And so I think 'The Vow' is maybe slowing things down a little bit, saying, 'Hey, let's see if we really can find love in this modern world.'" INSERT: CHRIS HARRISON SAYS YOUNG PEOPLE ARE REJECTING DATING APPS IN SEARCH OF SOMETHING 'MORE MEANINGFUL' The new series follows Jace Cates, a 30-year-old mortgage loan officer from Oregon, as he meets 10 women hoping to find a husband. Set in the Texas Hill Country, the show focuses on faith, family values and the possibility of building a lasting marriage. The first two episodes premiered Nov. 11, with new episodes scheduled to debut every Wednesday. For Harrison, returning to television with a project centered on relationships has been a rewarding experience. "If I'm being honest, it has felt very, very good to step back into the world of not just reality TV, but dating and love and helping people find love," he told Fox News Digital. "I just feel more than ever, we need love." Harrison said the early response to the series has been encouraging. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "But with the early returns that we have seen, the response from fans, people are loving it, and they seem to be enjoying the fact that I'm back on their TVs, which feels really good. It's kind of cathartic." The television personality explained that he wanted to create a dating experience that reflected the changing priorities he believes younger generations are embracing. "I think seeing the need for a show that is truly about love and romance, and seeing again this societal movement by the young people in this generation kind of asking for something deeper, more meaningful," he said. Harrison said he and the producers wanted to create an environment where participants could have serious conversations about their futures. "And so we've tried to make the most authentic, intentional environment so these people can really find love." The series has already sparked conversations about traditional marriage, with several women expressing interest in becoming stay-at-home mothers while others hope to continue pursuing their careers. Harrison said he welcomed the different perspectives, particularly because the contestants felt comfortable discussing their faith and expectations for marriage. "I'm really glad the ladies and Jace felt really comfortable speaking of their faith and speaking of what they want and hope in a marriage, in a family," he said. "They're asking those questions that you should be." He explained that the women represent a wide range of expectations for their future relationships. "There are some women that want to be stay-at-home moms. They want to just be a supportive wife. Then there are some that want to be CEOs and run the world." CHRIS HARRISON WEIGHS IN ON CONTROVERSY SURROUNDING TRADITIONAL MARRIAGE: 'IT'S GOING TO BE DIFFERENT FOR EVERYBODY' Harrison praised Jace for approaching the subject with an open mind. "And what I love about Jace is, when he was talking about what he thought about traditional marriage, it was all of that," he said. CHRIS HARRISON RETURNS TO REALITY TV WITH 'THE VOW,' FOX NATION'S FIRST-EVER DATING SHOW "It was just being a champion for my partner, just being there for my wife, whatever that looks like." The host acknowledged that the phrase "traditional marriage" can carry different meanings depending on the person. "Well, I think, you know, many things in this day and age become fragmented and political," he said. "And in this context, and I hope you'll watch 'The Vow,' because in this context, it really is more about faith and about their values and morals." Harrison said the show isn't meant to tell viewers what a marriage should look like, but rather to encourage conversations about what works for different couples. "I like leaning into the debate. I like leading into the conversation and maybe leaning into the uncomfortable a little bit, pushing ourselves." Faith also plays a central role in the series, with contestants openly discussing prayer, abstinence and their religious beliefs. Harrison said the decision to cast people of faith was intentional, but emphasized that the women have different perspectives when it comes to intimacy and relationships. "Some are kind of born again, celibate. Some are, you know, saving themselves," he said. He added that the variety of experiences allows viewers to connect with different contestants. "It's not just one size fits all. That's not the real world." Harrison also reflected on his own marriage to Lauren Zima, explaining that finding love when he least expected it reinforced his belief that people shouldn't give up on relationships. The couple recently celebrated their third wedding anniversary after exchanging vows in Napa Valley and later hosting a larger celebration in Austin, Texas. "Maybe that's the lesson, is never give up. When you least expect it, maybe expect it the most, but have faith," he said. "And I hope that's what 'The Vow' will do, is give people faith that love still exists." Harrison, who serves as an executive producer of the series alongside his wife, said working together has made the project especially meaningful. "You know, I think doing the show with the love of your life, first of all, it's an honor and a privilege to get to do that," he said. Ultimately, Harrison hopes the series encourages viewers to reconsider what they want from modern relationships. "What we're hearing from young people is that the bar is on the floor," he said. He explained that the goal was to raise expectations by focusing on genuine commitment rather than casual dating. "And the reaction so far has been, 'Thank you. Thank you for providing this environment. Thank you for doing a show like this.'" articles.summary: Actor Rasika Dugal says she is happy that \"Mirzapur: The Movie\" has given a much needed backstory to her character of Beena Tripathi, exploring her
articles.body: Actor Rasika Dugal says she is happy that "Mirzapur: The Movie" has given a much needed backstory to her character of Beena Tripathi, exploring her transformation into a manipulative and scheming person.Dugal has been part of "Mirzapur" series since its launch in 2018 and has consistently survived the violent world of crime over the next two seasons in 2020 and 2024.In the crime drama show, Beena is the second wife of Pankaj Tripathi's Akhandanand Tripathi, popularly known as Kaleen Bhaiya. She is shown trapped in a patriarchal household and has relied on manipulation and calculated moves to protect herself and retain her position in the family.The film, which explores an untold chapter from the inaugural season, delves into Beena's past relationship with a man named Birju (Mohitt Maalik)."I thought the film did a very beautiful job of giving Beena some context. I thought that was very interesting. We had, of course, thought of these things while we were shooting the series but it had not been etched out like this."And the whole angle with Birju (Raina), I think really was something which was very beautiful. That was one thing that I was sort of missing about Beena," Dugal told PTI.In the movie, which is streaming on Prime Video following its successful run in theatres, Beena ends up losing her first love in a tragic way, which gives context to many of her decisions in the show."Every season, very beautifully and very heartbreakingly, the show gives her agency and then takes it away. And then she tries to reclaim it and the film does the same, but with this context (of past love)," she added.Producer Farhan Akhtar, who was also part of the interview, called Beena the ultimate survivor in "Mirzapur" universe."The person who has the ultimate survival instinct, I think, is Beena and it reflects amazingly in the film," he said, adding that a key scene at the end of the movie will give viewers a glimpse into the character's psyche."Mirzapur: The Movie" released in theatres on September 4 and earned over Rs 300 crore at the box office. articles.title: Javed Akhtar slams music companies for interfering in creative process, says 'Give composers freedom'
articles.summary: Veteran lyricist and screenwriter Javed Akhtar has criticised the growing interference of producers and music companies in the creative process of film
articles.body: Veteran lyricist and screenwriter Javed Akhtar has criticised the growing interference of producers and music companies in the creative process of film music, saying that composers and lyricists are often not given enough freedom to do their work."If you don't trust a music director, then don't take him. If you trust him and he has talent, then give him a chance to do the music the way he wants to. For instance, look at the films where the music was scored by SD Burman, whom I admire greatly, like 'Chalti Ka Naam Gaadi', 'Sujata', and others, in every film (he) has a particular style, which suits the character and the film," Akhtar said at the launch of the Indian Performing Right Society's (IPRS) EY Music Creator Report.Drawing a parallel between filmmaking and music creation, the lyricist-writer said a film would lose its plot if different directors were brought in to shoot different kinds of scenes."If you have five directors in a film, like someone will shoot an emotional scene, and the light-hearted and romantic scene will be shot with some other director, then film will be messed," he added.Akhtar expressed concern over how music companies and producers often dictate terms to composers and lyric writers regarding a song."Somewhere we've moved away from the purpose. The problem is the tail is wagging the dog, that should not happen. There's too much interference, conditions. When a writer writes lyrics, they can do 100 times better work but they are not allowed to do so. Song writers like Irshad Kamal, and others are talented, but do you allow them to write good songs?" he asked.Recalling a personal instance of interference, Akhtar said an executive once objected to his use of the word 'roothna' in a song."Once a music composer owner told me, 'In the song, you've used the word 'roothana' don't do it as the song doesn't work'. So, then I gave example of four-five songs where 'roothana' word was there and they were a hit."But he said, 'Today, 'roothana' doesn't work', I said 'let someone else write the song, I'll not do it'."Akhtar said people with no understanding of music often dictate terms to songwriters and composers."Writing and music is something that everybody thinks, 'I understand it' but he doesn't understand so many other things, like physics, chemistry, geology but about music and writing they know it all. Like, they know what is good writing about, how to write, how not to write, what is the right word," he said.According to the (IPRS) EY report, India's music creator economy generated an estimated Rs. 17,400 crore in 2025, registering a 45 per cent increase since 2023.The sound recording and publishing revenues in 2025 reached Rs. 5,433 crore , an all time high. Besides, the annual releases of original songs increased to between 22,000 to 27,000 in 2025."We've come a long way and we've a long way to go also. But how much do the creators, the music directors, singers and writers, who produce music, get?"The rest of them are selling it, they are brokers and commission agents. Out of Rs. 5,000 crore, how much do the creators get? Not even Rs. 1,000 crore, so something is seriously wrong with the system," Akhtar said.The writer called for stronger implementation of copyright laws amid technological changes, including the growing use of artificial intelligence."Today, with technology one can patent voices. For instance, songs of Kishore Kumar are there everywhere but what is his family getting in return? Nothing. So, because of AI, there has to be international laws in place."And nationally, I should be thankful as we've conducive and considerate copyright laws in the country, but what about the implementation. Perhaps, only four percent of people are paying royalty from hotels, restaurants, bars, events, and so on. So, we should not celebrate thinking we've achieved so much," he said.Akhtar revealed that he and music composer-singer Shankar Mahadevan plan to hold an event next month via their company, Goongoonalo, which is India's first artist-owned and artist-led music platform and creative studio.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Dhanush thanks Tamil Nadu CM Vijay for 6 AM show permission for 'O.M', makes special request to fans
articles.summary: With his upcoming film 'O.M' set to arrive in theatres this Friday, Dhanush has shared a message for audiences, thanking them for their continued support
articles.body: With his upcoming film 'O.M' set to arrive in theatres this Friday, Dhanush has shared a message for audiences, thanking them for their continued support and urging them to celebrate the film's release responsibly. The actor-filmmaker also expressed gratitude to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay and the state government for permitting a 6 AM screening of the film.Dhanush thanks CM Vijay for 6 AM shows for 'O.M'Taking to X, Dhanush thanked the Tamil Nadu government and Chief Minister Vijay for allowing the early morning show ahead of the film's November 20 release. Sharing his appreciation, he wrote, "My heartfelt thanks to the Tamil Nadu government and the honourable Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Mr Vijay, for granting permission for the 6 AM show of 'OM', which is releasing on November 20."The permission comes following the state's revision of cinema regulations, which allows theatres to screen up to six shows a day, starting at 6 AM, during the first week of a new Tamil film's release. The move has brought back early morning screenings for major releases in the state.Dhanush asks fans to celebrate 'O.M' responsiblyAlong with thanking the government, Dhanush made a special appeal to fans who plan to attend the 6 AM screening. He urged them to prioritise safety and ensure their celebrations do not cause inconvenience to others. "I kindly request all fans attending the 6 AM show to remain safe, act responsibly, and avoid causing inconvenience to others. Enjoying the film is the real celebration," he wrote.The actor also highlighted how audiences can support the larger film industry by watching movies in theatres. He added, "The biggest support you can give everyone working in the film industry is to visit theatres and watch films, thereby contributing to the growth of cinema." He ended his message by expressing his love and gratitude to fans.Mammootty and Sai Pallavi star alongside Dhanush in 'O.M'Written and directed by Rajkumar Periasamy, who previously helmed 'Amaran', 'O.M: Chapter 1 – Udhiram: The Blood Wood' is a crime thriller centred on a police operation against a red sandalwood smuggling network. Dhanush plays an undercover Tamil Nadu Special Task Force officer, while Sai Pallavi portrays an IPS officer leading the investigation. articles.title: Wondering why your friends are MIA? ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ might be to blame
articles.summary: Between spikes in vacation day requests and college professors reportedly granting extensions to their students, the Thursday release of Grand Theft Auto VI could bring America (or the world) to a halt.
articles.body: Between spikes in vacation day requests and college professors reportedly granting extensions to their students, the Thursday release of Grand Theft Auto VI could bring America (or the world) to a halt. GTA VI, which will be available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, is the first release in the Grand Theft Auto series since 2013. Rockstar Games, the publisher behind the company, reportedly spent more than $1 billion to simply make the game. That’s more than the rumored budgets of the upcoming “Avengers” and “Dune” movies combined. As of Wednesday, the game has notched a whopping 99/100 on Metacritic, which distills reviews from around the Internet. That ties it with Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time for highest rated game of all time. Here’s everything you need to know about why GTA VI is shaping up to be one of the biggest cultural events of the year. The game made $1.5 billion in prelaunch sales GTA VI is the eighth entry in the main Grand Theft Auto series, which doesn’t include spinoffs and expansion packs. The series began with Grand Theft Auto in 1997, but entered a new era in 2001 with the release of Grand Theft Auto III, the first in the series to feature a three-dimensional world. Since then, Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto: Vice City in 2002, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas in 2004, Grand Theft Auto IV in 2008 and Grand Theft Auto V in 2013. The 13-year gap between V and VI is the longest wait between games in the main series. In 2025, more than a full year before the release of the game, the second trailer for GTA VI racked up more than 475 million views, Rockstar told The Hollywood Reporter at the time. The company ramped up its promotion this year by partnering with Netflix to release a 27-minute video of gameplay on the streaming service. The extended look drew 31.1 million viewers in one weekend. That’s more than the 2026 average viewership of “Sunday Night Football.” As of Tuesday, the game, which costs $79.99 for the standard edition, has sold nearly 16 million copies, earning Rockstar more than $1.5 billion already, according to SensorTower, an analytics company that tracks market performance in the gaming industry. Why do fans care so much? “It’s a really good question,” said Bart Spiegel, the global media, entertainment, gaming and sports keader at PricewaterhouseCoopers, one of the world‘s “Big Four” professional service firms. “The easiest way to explain is it’s been 13 years in the making, and they spent over a billion dollars. So it’s really about the level of effort that’s gone into this game, and just everybody waiting for it.” Even before its release, GTA’s latest installment was recognized as a nominee in the game of the year category for the upcoming Game Awards, which are being held in December. Nominees were chosen by a global jury of more than 100 media publications and creators. Geoff Keighley, the CEO of The Game Awards, was not surprised that the Rockstar game made the cut, despite not being released to the general public yet. “What makes the game so unique is its scale and ambition, and the freedom it gives players to explore a simulated virtual world,” he wrote in an email to NBC News. People are already canceling their plans to play To Keighley’s point, what’s allowed for the Grand Theft Auto series to endure is the freedom and playable hours it affords consumers. Completing the game’s missions will likely take around 50 hours, according to the publication Insider Gaming. But completing every single side task to pursue “platinum” status could push playtime up to 200 hours. And that doesn’t include time players can spend in the game’s world doing a variety of activities of their choosing, which include but are not limited to: working out, gambling, scuba diving, petting animals, going to a strip club, hijacking cars, jetskiing, robbing banks and even watching television. For the first time in the game’s history, players will be allowed to toggle between the perspectives of Jason (a male) and Lucia (a female), who exhibit a Bonnie-and-Clyde dynamic as the player follows their story. Simply put, playing through GTA VI can be a weekslong commitment if someone wants it to be. And that is almost definitely selling it short. Miami leans into its alter ego: Vice City The story of GTA VI takes place in the fictional Vice City, seemingly the most thinly veiled representation of Miami. Other locations on the game’s map are inspired by the Everglades and the Florida Keys. The game’s first trailer, which was released in 2023 and set to Tom Petty’s “Love is a Long Road,” contained several references to incidents from Florida. The city of Miami has not shied away from the game, accepting an advertisement package from Rockstar for $3.9 million. “With millions of people around the world waiting for this release, we have an opportunity to make sure Miami-Dade benefits from that attention,” Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava said in October. “These agreements allow us to turn that excitement into additional revenue for our community.” Among those participating are the NBA’s Miami Heat, who will play on a special, Vice City-themed court at their home arena Wednesday. The Heat also partnered with Rockstar on a merch drop, and the roof of the three-time NBA champion’s arena is emblazoned with the words, “Welcome to Vice City.” Rockstar employees told Dazed magazine that it took years of on-the-ground exploration in Florida to shape the game’s world. A team of almost 5,000 people worked on the game, according to The Guardian, with a lot of attention being put into the details. Rockstar even built a studio dedicated entirely to the look and behavior of nonplayable characters (NPCs) — those are characters players don’t even control and only sometimes interact with. You can even buy the game just to look at birds, of which there more than 62 species. “We will meet with ex-criminals, law enforcement, club promoters, gun dealers and anyone notorious or influential who’ll take our calls,” Rupert Humphries, Rockstar’s senior vice president of narrative, said. “We hang out, get a feeling for the place, listen to the stories, cross-reference that with books and journalism, and try to get to the heart of which characters will bring the city we are creating to life.” The developers said year that this GTA VI world will be “more grounded and reactive than before,” meaning nonplayer characters will react appropriately to players who walk down the street with rifles. GTA VI will also feature changes in the protagonists’ physical condition akin to the system in Rockstar’s acclaimed Red Dead Redemption 2. That means, for example, Jason and Lucia can gain or lose weight, build muscle and incur physical markers of exhaustion. ‘One of the biggest entertainment events of the decade’ GTA VI is expected to not only cross cultural lines, but also generational ones. “The average gamer age is like high 30s to low 40s or something like that. Don’t think it’s just 18-year-old, 19-year-old, or teenage boys that are going to be playing,” Spiegel said. “You’re going to see this across all demographics.” His own son was only 6 when the last GTA came out. Now that he’s 19, Spiegel said, he’s as excited to play as his dad is. The gaming industry, which has in recent years been hit with massive layoffs, also has high hopes for the game. GTA VI leads the pack of Game Awards nominees, racking eight total nods. “I expect [GTA VI] to be one of the biggest entertainment events of the decade,” Keighley said, noting the game’s “reach goes well beyond those holding the controller.” “People will encounter it through livestreams, clips, music and conversations with friends,” he said. “That’s what makes this such a significant moment: a game can become the thing everyone is talking about.”
