articles.title: The lead actress in ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ has finally been revealed. What to know about the woman behind Lucia.
articles.summary: Manni L. Perez once said her "biggest fear" was playing a "damsel in distress." Her character in the year's most-anticipated game is anything but helpless.
articles.body:
There are a lot of things players can do in Grand Theft Auto VI that weren't possible in previous editions of the franchise. One of the most notable is that they can play as Lucia, the first major female protagonist in the history of the series.

Iconic female main characters have been a staple of video games from the beginning (see: Ms. Pac-Man, Samus Aran, etc.), but the presence of a complex, fully fleshed-out woman at the core of GTA 6 's story represents a significant change for a franchise that has been accused in the past of treating female side characters as equal parts eye candy and cannon fodder.

In the lead-up to the game's release, most of its sprawling cast of voice actors had remained a mystery. That's still true of nearly all of its main characters. But the voice behind Lucia was seemingly confirmed on Tuesday when the Game Awards announced that Manni L. Perez had been nominated for Best Performance for her voice work in the game. GTA 6 received eight nominations in total, including Game of the Year.

The revelation came as little surprise to die-hard GTA fans, who had speculated for months that the little-known American actor was the voice behind one half of the game's core duo. GTA 6 's story centers around Lucia and her boyfriend Jason, a pair of outlaws trying to make their mark in a cartoonishly criminal knockoff of Miami called Vice City. The actor who plays Jason is still unknown.

The limited information we have about Perez's personal bio comes from her own recent social media statements and a few dated news stories.

While deftly dodging a deluge of questions from GTA fans asking her to confirm her role in the game on Instagram Live last month, she described herself as having grown up in a "small, rural, rednecky hick town" roughly three hours from New York, where she now lives. "We grew up very lower middle class," she added. She said she has family in Harlem and is reportedly of Puerto Rican and Dominican descent.

According to a 2018 interview with Paz Magazine, Perez studied at New York University's prestigious Tisch School of the Arts. She said she initially wanted to pursue a career as a professional belly dancer before being convinced to try acting by a college professor. Perez is also an avid weightlifter and has practiced a variety of martial arts, including Muay Thai and Brazilian jiu-jitsu.

"I have a very specific niche in the industry," she told the magazine. "A lot of the roles I get called in for require me to be fit, strong, and kick ass."

Perez has played a series of minor TV roles in recent years, including guest appearances on J essica Jones , Chicago P.D. and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit .

On Instagram, she told her followers that her modest acting success so far hasn't yet fundamentally changed her life.

"I live in a small studio apartment, which I love," she said. "I have my tiny, little itty-bitty kitchen, and it's just me and my dog. I do everything on my own, and I've done everything on my own for a very long time, and I love it, and I'm very grateful."

GTA 6 is her breakout role, but it isn't the first work she's done with the franchise. She was credited as the voice of Clubber #2 in Grand Theft Auto V and as an unnamed blackjack dealer in a 2019 update to Grand Theft Auto Online .

One comment Perez made to Paz Magazine eight years ago turned out to be remarkably prescient about the role that would turn into a major star in the video game world.

"To be honest, my biggest fear is to play a woman that needs to be saved by a man," she said. "Like, I can't imagine playing the damsel in distress. … I'd prefer to play a character that, whatever she's going through, no matter how hard society wants to keep her down, she picks herself up, puts her big girl panties on (preferably cotton) and keeps it moving."

What do we know about the rest of the cast?

Very little. Fans have speculated that Lucia's partner, Jason Duval, is played by actor Dylan Rourke , who's appeared in Grey's Anatomy and Modern Family , but Rockstar has not confirmed that. More rumors abound about the other actors who voice the game's key characters, but so far only one other cast member has been officially announced.

Celebrated comedic actor Stephen Root , who recently won an Emmy for his supporting role on Widow's Bay , has confirmed that he'll play a criminal named Brian Heder, who GTA 6's character guide describes as "a classic drug runner from the golden age of smuggling."

articles.title: Skydance CEO David Ellison pressed about his politics, CBS and CNN’s futures at NYT DealBook Summit
articles.summary: Skydance CEO David Ellison appeared at The New York Times DealBook Summit and was asked about the futures of CBS News and CNN, among other things.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Skydance CEO David Ellison was in the hot seat Wednesday at The New York Times DealBook Summit, making his first major appearance since the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) merger. Sitting down with The New York Times' Andrew Ross Sorkin, Ellison reiterated his mission for both CBS News and CNN to provide "truth-based, fact-based bipartisan down the middle" coverage, in the aftermath of closing his $111 billion purchase of WBD, putting two major Hollywood studios and dozens of networks, including HBO, CBS and CNN, under one corporate umbrella. "When you look at what our goal for news is — we're one year into this journey — is to make sure that we can rebuild trust back to at least where it was previously, if not even higher," Ellison said. "We have incredible journalists that are showing up every single day to accomplish that goal. That is our mission today. That is a mission tomorrow. That will be our mission five years from now." "And fundamentally, we will not stop working until we earn that trust. And from an editorial standpoint, you know, we believe in editorial independence, we don't get involved basically in those decisions, but we trust the journalists to do their jobs," he continued. CNN STAFFERS ACCEPT NEW REALITY AS PARAMOUNT'S TAKEOVER OF WARNER BROS DISCOVERY GOES FULL STEAM AHEAD The consolidation sparked major concerns within the media and entertainment industry, particularly how he intends to oversee both CBS News and CNN. He has overseen CBS News since late 2025 after Skydance's $8 billion merger with Paramount. Ellison was asked whether CBS News and CNN will merge as a result of corporate synergy. He teased about potential changes to come but kept details under wraps. "Right now, we're incredibly happy operating on basically within the status quo," Ellison said. "There might be some news-sharing in the future, but right now we're happy with them with where they are." The Skydance chief sidestepped questions about his appointment of Bari Weiss as the editor-in-chief of CBS News and the major shakeups at "60 Minutes," namely Scott Pelley's dramatic exit from the magazine program earlier this year, telling Sorkin he's "really proud" of the work of his journalists. BARI WEISS AT CBS NEWS: A YEAR OF DRAMA AND CHALLENGES AS SHE ATTEMPTS TO REVAMP THE TIFFANY NETWORK Critics of Ellison and his billionaire father Larry Ellison, who provided financial backing for the multibillion-dollar merger, have taken aim over the Ellisons' perceived chumminess with President Donald Trump. When asked directly by Sorkin whether he himself voted for Trump, Ellison dodged. "I've actually never disclosed that," Ellison responded. "And what I'll say is for me, I voted both sides of the aisle basically my entire life... I'm not a partisan." He noted that, "Half my family's Democrat, half my family is Republican," adding that such dynamics "could make dinner table conversations a little bit challenging." CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS Ellison also dispelled the rumors that Paramount's development of "Rush Hour 4" was not because of Trump's demand but rather one of his studio chiefs who came up with reviving the Jackie Chan-Chris Tucker franchise. "You never heard from your father or from the president on anything about 'Rush Hour 4,' that's completely a made-up story," Sorkin followed. "There's a lot of made-up stories," Ellison replied. Ellison was also asked about Elon Musk's billion-dollar investment into Skydance. He refrained from saying whether there will be a more formal partnership with the SpaceX founder in the future but said any collaboration would "be a privilege." Ellison also committed that HBO will distribute "Musk," the scathing documentary about the tech mogul produced by A24, which has a streaming partnership with HBO. "We believe in independence. We don't believe in censorship of any kind," Ellison said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Absolute Batman can save DC Studios
articles.summary: Skydance should be looking to DC’s Absolute comics line as it maps out the DCU’s future.
articles.body: With James Gunn and Peter Safran out as the co-heads of DC Studios following Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, it’s unclear what will become of the cinematic universe that was building around movies like last year’s Superman. Though Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow feature might still come out, it seems like his larger vision for the DC Universe may be tossed out by DC Studios’ newly appointed CEO, Jeremy Latcham. Gunn was taking his time fleshing out the DCU with relatively less high-profile characters like Peacemaker, Supergirl, and Clayface. But Latcham has reportedly received a mandate from Skydance CEO David Ellison to fast-track a new version of the Justice League featuring more popular heroes like Wonder Woman and the Green Lantern. This drastic shift in priorities will likely change what the DCU looks like in the coming years as Skydance attempts to parlay its comics IP into projects that can help it get on top of the $80 billion of debt the company is now responsible for after acquiring WBD. Ellison’s instinct to whip out the A-list superheroes is probably right from a business perspective. Most casual DC movie fans are more interested in stories about the Trinity than obscure characters like Gorilla Grodd. But after two iffy attempts at creating interconnected DC movie franchises, that audience might not have much of an appetite for yet another full-on reboot. Rather than starting from scratch, DC Studios should probably keep some of the things that worked well during Gunn and Safran’s tenure, like presenting Superman as a compassionate person with a strong moral compass. But if the studio really wants to take this franchise in a new direction that gets people excited, it should also be thinking about tapping into the energy of some of DC’s most successful recent comics. Though the WBD merger prompted Skydance to begin laying off almost 2,000 employees last month, DC Comics — which Skydance gained control of as part of the deal — was reportedly left unscathed because the publishing arm’s business has been performing surprisingly well. Much of that success seems to have been driven by strong sales of comics created by DC’s Absolute Universe imprint. [Image: Launched in 2024, the Absolute Universe comics reimagine DC’s heroes and villains as wildly different versions of their classic selves. Absolute Wonder Woman is a witch raised in Hell, Absolute Superman first arrives on Earth as a teenager who remembers his childhood on Krypton, and Absolute Batman is a working-class civil engineer rather than a socialite born into immense wealth. The Absolute characters’ worldviews and approaches to enacting justice are all distinct from their mainstream universe counterparts. But as much as the Absolute comics diverge from established canon, they each capture the essence of what makes their central characters iconic pillars of the DC brand. Wonder Woman aside, there have been so many cinematic portrayals of DC characters based on their classic selves that it has often seemed like Warner Bros. was stuck in a kind of rut. There have been slight stylistic differences between the various big-screen iterations of Superman and Batman over the years, but for the most part, they have all come across as the products of a studio that’s averse to trying new things. That’s part of what made Matt Reeves’ The Batman — which didn’t bother to rehash Bruce Wayne’s tragic origin story — feel somewhat like a breath of fresh air when it debuted in 2022. Robert Pattinson will reprise his role as the Dark Knight in The Batman Part II, but it’s not really clear whether that version of the character will have any bearing on the DCU’s future. Between Reeves’ Batman films existing in their own universe (similar to Todd Phillips’ Joker features) and Pattinson presumably being busy now that he’s been cast as Amazon’s new James Bond, it doesn’t seem likely that that version of the character will be incorporated into the DCU. Ellison obviously intends to put out more projects featuring Batman, though, and DC Studios could tell a riveting story if it took some cues from the hero’s Absolute incarnation. What makes Absolute Batman such a compelling series is the way it inverts the established power structures that define most classic Batman comics. In those books, Bruce Wayne is part of Gotham’s marginalized underclass, while the Joker is a moneyed elite whose villainy is highlighted in the way he manipulates various industries. [Image: [Image: [Image: This inversion puts Absolute Batman in a position to operate as a vigilante with a much deeper connection to the ordinary people he has sworn to protect. Monstrous supervillains like Poison Ivy and Bane are still major threats, but the comics also spend time pitting Absolute Batman against more ordinary evils like corrupt police departments infested with white nationalists fixated on terrorizing minorities. Absolute Batman’s progressive political overtones might not gel with Ellison’s personal sensibilities, and the comic’s brutality probably doesn’t align with Latcham’s approach to making films. But Absolute Batman’s phenomenal sales have made it abundantly clear that readers are enjoying these stories, which is likely a big part why DC Studios announced earlier this year that it has plans to produce an animated series based on the comics. Those plans might change in the wake of Skydance acquiring WBD, but an Absolute Batman series would give DC Studios an organic way to introduce the character into its tentpole films. Having characters jump back and forth between TV and the big screen was one of the stronger ideas Gunn introduced to the DCU, and it’s a strategy that could continue to benefit DC Studios under Latcham’s leadership. Turning Absolute Batman into the next flagship Bruce Wayne would be a bold move on Skydance’s part. But if the studio really wants to prove that this megamerger was the right decision, it needs to show the public that it has the guts to take exciting chances.

articles.title: Candela Peña reconoce que lloró con la entrevista a Abascal y compara a David Broncano con las mujeres: "Fallas y te vas a tomar por culo"
articles.standfirst: La colaboradora de ‘La Revuelta’ ha defendido a su compañero por lo ocurrido tras la charla con el candidato de VOX
articles.summary: La colaboradora de ‘La Revuelta’ ha defendido a su compañero por lo ocurrido tras la charla con el candidato de VOX
articles.body: Este miércoles, 18 de septiembre, RTVE ha vuelto a emitir un nuevo programa de ‘La Revuelta’, formato presentado por David Broncano que ha estado rodeado de polémica durante la semana por la visita de Abascal. Este es el último programa de esta semana por la celebración del debate electoral entre Feijóo y Pedro Sánchez. Relacionado con este asunto, por el espacio de Broncano han pasado el líder del PSOE, el de VOX, Ada Colau, Gabriel Rufián e Irene Montero. Candela Peña, como colaboradora, sólo coincidió con el presidente del Gobierno, pero realmente se le quedó marcada la entrevista a Abascal. Eso sí, desde el punto de vista negativo. Antes de hablar de la parte más polémica, ha valorado el trabajo de su compañero en RTVE: “Eres una persona que lo intenta, buscas la cohesión, la convivencia y pides perdón. Es todo lo que un ser humano ha de tener”. Incluso, la colaboradora ha reconocido que lloró por todo el revuelo generado en las horas posteriores. La actriz y cómica no entiende las críticas que vertieron sobre David Broncano por parte de las redes sociales y medios de comunicación. Además, cuenta que lo pasó realmente mal con la entrevista. “No eres periodista, pero tampoco lo eres cuando viene Bardem, Pedro Sánchez u otras personalidades”, ha defendido Peña. Del mismo modo, ha reconocido que mientras veía la charla con Abascal, Broncano le recordó a las mujeres. Cuando el presentador le ha preguntado por qué, ella ha sido contundente: “David, no se nos permite fallar. Fallas y te vas a tomar por culo”. La colaboradora de ‘La Revuelta’ ha hablado también de la polarización que vive España en estos tiempos políticos, dejando esta reflexión al respecto: “En misa, me encuentro y cohabito con gente que piensa completamente diferente a mí. Los quiere profundamente. Yo estoy enamorada de un señor que es de derechas, que no me hace ni pu** caso, quizás es por eso. No me preguntes por él porque está casado”.

The film earned Rs 2.65 cr net in India on Day 13, registering an 8.6% decline from the previous day's Rs 2.90 cr.The Jithu Madhavan directorial collected Rs 1.85 cr from Tamil screenings and Rs 80 lakh from Telugu shows. The domestic earnings came from a total of 3,962 screenings across both languages. The latest figures take its cumulative India net collection to Rs 145.05 cr, while the domestic gross stands at Rs 168.50 cr.'Scene' worldwide box office collection reaches Rs 256.50 crAccording to Sacnilk, the film added Rs 1 cr through overseas markets on its 13th day. This takes its total international gross collection to Rs 88 cr. Its worldwide gross has now reached Rs 256.50 cr.The film's domestic net collection comprises Rs 116 cr from the Tamil version and Rs 29.05 cr from Telugu screenings. Tamil accounts for 80% of the India net total, while Telugu contributes the remaining 20%. The domestic market represents 65.7% of the worldwide gross, with overseas territories providing 34.3%.'Scene' witnessed a limited decline in its daily earnings compared with Tuesday. Its India net collection moved from Rs 2.90 cr on Day 12 to Rs 2.65 cr on Wednesday. The film's second-week performance has added to its overall domestic total.During its opening week, covering the first seven days, the movie collected Rs 111.70 cr net and Rs 129.75 cr gross in India. The subsequent six days contributed another Rs 33.35 cr net and Rs 38.75 cr gross. Together, these earnings have taken the domestic collection to Rs 145.05 cr net.The Tamil version remained the primary contributor to the film's daily business. Its Rs 1.85 cr collection accounted for 69.8% of the day's total India net earnings. Telugu screenings contributed the remaining Rs 80 lakh.Tamil shows registered an overall occupancy of 18.44%. Morning screenings recorded 14.38%, while the afternoon occupancy stood at 18.38%. The figure improved to 19.92% during evening shows and reached 21.08% at night.The Telugu version registered 11.91% overall occupancy. Morning shows recorded 10.73%, followed by 11% in the afternoon. Evening occupancy stood at 9.73%, while night screenings registered 12.91%.Tamil Nadu leads state-wise box office collectionTamil Nadu emerged as the biggest contributor among the tracked Indian markets on Day 13. The state generated Rs 1.40 cr in gross collections, accounting for 45.9% of the combined state-wise total of Rs 3.05 cr.Andhra Pradesh and Telangana together contributed Rs 80 lakh. Kerala added Rs 50 lakh, while Karnataka recorded Rs 30 lakh. The remaining Indian markets accounted for another Rs 5 lakh.Suriya, Nazriya Nazim headline Jithu Madhavan's film'Scene' features Suriya and Nazriya Nazim in the lead roles, alongside Naslen K. Gafoor, Lal and Anandraj. The film marks the first collaboration between Suriya and director Jithu Madhavan.Vineeth Augustian handled the cinematography, while Sushin Shyam composed the music. Ajmal Sabu worked as the editor. With its worldwide gross now at Rs 256.50 cr, the film continues its theatrical run as it moves towards the Rs 300 cr mark.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. articles.title: CMA Awards 2026 live updates: Taylor Swift, Ella Langley, Lainey Wilson and Stella Lefty dazzle on red carpet
articles.summary: Ella Langley! Taylor Swift! Chris Stapleton! The 2026 CMA Awards is taking Nashville by storm.
articles.body: All eyes are on Nashville for country music's biggest night of the year: the 60th CMA Awards. For the third year in a row, country crooner Lainey Wilson is hosting the ceremony, pulling double duty as a performer alongside big names like Ella Langley, Chris Stapleton, Miranda Lambert, Kacey Musgraves, Luke Combs, Tim McGraw and — in her first CMAs performance since 2013 and first appearance at the show since 2016 — Taylor Swift. Airing live on ABC and Disney+, the show is capping what's been a major year for country music, between Langley's record-breaking hit "Choosin' Texas" dominating the airwaves and Swift herself making a long-awaited return to the genre with "I Knew It, I Knew You" from Toy Story 5. Keep reading our live blog below to catch all the action unfolding in Music City tonight, from the big winners to the buzziest boot-stomping performances.
